user_story: As a developer, I run `starlog search "<capability>"` to see ranked candidate packages.
expected_behaviour: Prints a table (#, Library, Category, Score, Solves) of up to 5 results ranked by the local keyword ranker with MMR diversity (lambda 0.5); scores are absolute; exit 0.

user_story: As a tool builder, I run `starlog search <q> --format json` to get machine-readable results.
expected_behaviour: Prints a pretty-printed JSON array of QueryResult objects (manifest, relevance_score, vs_custom, context_fit, tradeoffs) on stdout; nothing else on stdout; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, I mistype `--format xml` and expect a clear error.
expected_behaviour: Prints `Invalid format: xml. Use "json" or "table".` and exits 1.

user_story: As a user, I pass `--category doesnotexist` and still want results.
expected_behaviour: Warns `Note: "..."  is not a known category (...)` listing known categories, then searches the whole corpus anyway; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, I filter with `--category caching` to only see caching libraries.
expected_behaviour: Only manifests whose category exactly matches are returned.

user_story: As a user, I filter `--stack react` and must not get react-native-only libraries.
expected_behaviour: stack_affinity is matched case-insensitively but exactly (no substring); non-matching manifests are excluded.

user_story: As a user, I pass `--top-k 2` to cap the result count.
expected_behaviour: At most 2 results print; a non-numeric value falls back to the default 5.

user_story: As a user with an out-of-corpus query, I want an honest miss, not a forced answer.
expected_behaviour: stderr explains no strong match + lists covered categories + points at `starlog facts` / `corpus add`; exit 0. With `--format json`, stdout still gets `[]` so jq pipelines parse.

user_story: As a user whose query matched a stray keyword, I should see it's low confidence.
expected_behaviour: When exactly 1 result scores < 70 (table mode), stderr prints 'No strong match ... Closest by keyword:' before the table.

user_story: As a power user, I pass `--diversity 1` for pure relevance order.
expected_behaviour: lambda >= 1.0 disables MMR (pure score-descending); lower values trade relevance for diversity; displayed scores always monotonic descending.

user_story: As a user, I pass `--context` to get a per-library vs-custom rationale.
expected_behaviour: With an LLM available (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) top results gain vs_custom/tradeoffs; without a key search still works and fields stay empty (never crashes).

user_story: As an org developer, my internal package (STARLOG_PRIVATE_CORPUS) should surface first for a matching capability.
expected_behaviour: Relevant (score>=70) private manifests are floated ahead of public results; off-topic private manifests are not floated; private wins on id collision.

user_story: As a keyed user with a broken network, search must still work.
expected_behaviour: With STARLOG_API_KEY set and the API unreachable, stderr notes the fallback and results come from the bundled corpus; keyless users never touch the network.

user_story: As a developer, I run `starlog facts ua-parser-js` to vet a package before using it.
expected_behaviour: Prints layered markdown: header, effect surface, capabilities, maintenance, license (risk), known vulns/incidents, transitive risk, source, and a dated 'Verified: as of' line; exit 0.

user_story: As a developer, I look up a package with no record and want an honest answer.
expected_behaviour: Prints 'No facts on file for ...' with guidance (npm audit/OSV, `starlog facts add` for internal packages); exit 0 (a miss is not an error).

user_story: As a tool builder, I run `starlog facts <pkg> --format json` for the raw layers.
expected_behaviour: Prints a JSON object with independent l1/l2/l3 layers (or `null` on a miss); exit 0.

user_story: As a user, I mistype the format flag.
expected_behaviour: Prints `Invalid format: ... Use "json" or "table".`; exit 1.

user_story: As a user, `starlog facts express-rate-limit` must never return facts about `express`.
expected_behaviour: Resolution is exact (lowercase+trim only); near-miss names return the honest 'No facts on file' message, never another package's facts.

user_story: As an org developer, facts for my internal package come from STARLOG_PRIVATE_FACTS.
expected_behaviour: A valid `{l1,l2}` file adds/overrides facts per layer (private wins); the composed view renders like any public fact.

user_story: As an org developer, a package with an L3 rule shows the org verdict.
expected_behaviour: With STARLOG_POLICY set, `**Org policy:** ALLOW/DENY/FLAG — rationale (rule id)` renders at the top of the fact view.

user_story: As an org admin, a ban on a package with no facts record must still surface.
expected_behaviour: A package matched only by a policy rule (no L1/L2) still composes a view showing the verdict instead of silently no-opping.

user_story: As a user with a malformed private-facts file, facts must still serve public data.
expected_behaviour: stderr warns 'private facts file unreadable ... using public facts only'; lookup proceeds with public layers; never throws.

user_story: As an org developer, `starlog facts add @acme/pkg --status active --license MIT` makes it vet clean.
expected_behaviour: Writes/creates .starlog/private-facts.json with a schema-valid L2 overlay (source 'hand', fetched_at today); prints the path + guidance on how the agent reads it; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, re-running facts add for the same package updates it without duplicating.
expected_behaviour: Same-package l2 entry replaced; other l2 entries and any l1 array preserved.

user_story: As a user, a bad `--status` or `--license-risk` should fail loudly with the valid options.
expected_behaviour: stderr `starlog: facts add failed: Invalid --status ... use one of: active, maintenance-only, deprecated, abandoned, compromised`; exit 1; nothing written.

user_story: As a user, I record a vuln with `--vuln id:severity:summary` (summary may contain colons).
expected_behaviour: Splits on the first two colons only; invalid severity lists valid ones and exits 1; repeatable flag accumulates.

user_story: As a user with STARLOG_PRIVATE_FACTS set, facts add writes there and tells me the caveat.
expected_behaviour: Writes to the env path and prints the note that init wires only the default path (custom path read by CLI only).

user_story: As a user with a broken private-facts.json, facts add must not silently overwrite it.
expected_behaviour: SyntaxError surfaces as `invalid JSON — ... Fix or remove the malformed file, then retry.`; exit 1; original file untouched.

user_story: As an org developer, `starlog corpus add @acme/flags --solves ...` makes search surface it.
expected_behaviour: Writes .starlog/private-corpus.json with a schema-valid manifest (honest zero-value health defaults); prints guidance + the tip to also `facts add`; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, omitting --solves must fail with the reason it matters.
expected_behaviour: Commander requiredOption error (exit 1); nothing written.

user_story: As a user, a bad `--effort` or `--ecosystem` fails with valid options.
expected_behaviour: Clear 'Invalid --effort/--ecosystem ... use one of: ...' error; exit 1.

user_story: As an org admin, `starlog facts policy lodash deny --reason ...` records a rule.
expected_behaviour: Writes/upserts .starlog/policy.json rule `pkg-<name>` with the rationale; prints how to make the agent apply it (export STARLOG_POLICY) or confirms it's already read; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, `starlog facts policy pkg maybe` should fail.
expected_behaviour: stderr `Invalid verdict "maybe" — use one of: allow, deny, flag`; exit 1.

user_story: As an admin, re-setting a verdict replaces the old rule, never duplicates.
expected_behaviour: Rule id `pkg-<name>` is stable; org field and unrelated rules preserved.

user_story: As a user writing to an unwritable path, I get an actionable message, not a stack trace.
expected_behaviour: EACCES/EPERM → `permission denied (<path>). Try a path you own or re-run with appropriate permissions.`; exit 1.

user_story: As an org admin, `starlog org sync <dir>` derives facts for every published package in one pass.
expected_behaviour: Scans immediate subdirectories with package.json or pyproject.toml; writes private-facts.json (L2, source 'analyzer'), private-corpus.json (discovery), policy.suggested.json; summary lines report counts; exit 0.

user_story: As an admin, repos with no published name are reported, never fabricated.
expected_behaviour: Skipped count includes them; no synthetic keys are written.

user_story: As an admin, packages without a description are vettable but not discoverable and I'm told how to fix.
expected_behaviour: Summary lists them: 'have no description, so they are vettable but NOT discoverable ... Add a description'.

user_story: As an admin, derived flags (copyleft-strong, unknown license, deprecated/abandoned) go to a separate suggestion file the agent never reads.
expected_behaviour: policy.suggested.json regenerated fresh each run; output says PROPOSALS and points at `starlog facts policy <pkg> flag` to adopt.

user_story: As an admin with the same package in two checkouts, I'm warned which one won.
expected_behaviour: `Warning: "<pkg>" was derived from N checkouts (...); kept the last.` printed; last one wins.

user_story: As an admin, re-running sync must preserve hand-authored facts for other packages.
expected_behaviour: Existing l2 entries for packages not in this sync are preserved; same-package entries are refreshed.

user_story: As an admin pointing at the wrong dir, I get a clear error.
expected_behaviour: `org sync: no checkouts found under <dir> (looked for immediate subdirectories containing a package.json or pyproject.toml).`; exit 1.

user_story: As an admin without git history, maintenance falls back to active.
expected_behaviour: With --no-git, lastCommitDaysAgo is null and maintenance defaults to 'active'.

user_story: As an admin, a repo untouched for 6/18 months is graded honestly.
expected_behaviour: last commit >=180 days → maintenance-only; >=540 days → abandoned; archived/deprecated → deprecated.

user_story: As a user, `starlog init` must show me every change and ask before writing.
expected_behaviour: Prints planned changes ([+ create]/[~ update]/[= ok]/[- skip] with paths), then asks 'Apply these changes? [y/N]'; in a non-interactive shell it stops with 're-run with --yes' and writes nothing.

user_story: As a cautious user, I preview without writing.
expected_behaviour: Plan prints then 'Dry run — no changes written.'; no files touched.

user_story: As a CI user, `starlog init --yes` wires everything unattended.
expected_behaviour: ~/.claude/settings.json gains mcpServers.starlog (node dist/mcp.js with per-project STARLOG_PRIVATE_* env) and a PostToolUse Bash hook entry; hook script written to ~/.claude/hooks/starlog-pkg-check.js; post-install summary printed.

user_story: As a user, running init twice must not duplicate or rewrite anything.
expected_behaviour: Second run shows all [= ok] and 'Everything is already configured. No changes needed.'

user_story: As a user, `starlog init --project --yes` drops a marked Starlog section in CLAUDE.md.
expected_behaviour: Section delimited by <!-- starlog:init --> / <!-- starlog:end --> appended; drifted bounded sections are refreshed in place; user content preserved.

user_story: As a user without Cursor/Copilot/Codex, init skips them with a reason; --all forces.
expected_behaviour: Undetected agents show `[- skip] <agent> — <reason> (use --all to force)`; with --all their instruction files are planned/written.

user_story: As an org user, `starlog init --api-key K --yes` wires the key into the MCP env.
expected_behaviour: settings.json mcpServers.starlog.env.STARLOG_API_KEY === K; summary says 'Ranking mode: hosted'; exported STARLOG_API_KEY works too.

user_story: As a user, `starlog init --uninstall` removes everything Starlog added and backs up edited files.
expected_behaviour: MCP entry + hook (file & registration) removed; marked sections removed from CLAUDE.md/copilot-instructions/AGENTS.md with .bak backups reported; Cursor rule deleted; unrelated settings preserved.

user_story: As a user with broken settings.json, init must not clobber it.
expected_behaviour: init fails with `Failed to parse ~/.claude/settings.json: ...`; exit 1; file untouched.

user_story: As a user running from the npx cache, I'm warned the wired paths will break.
expected_behaviour: When package root is under _npx, the summary warns and suggests `npm install -g starloghq && starlog init`.

user_story: As a user who just `npm i starloghq`, I learn install alone wires nothing.
expected_behaviour: postinstall prints one bold line pointing at `npx starlog init`; silent in CI / non-TTY / silent loglevel; never fails the install.

user_story: As a Claude Code user who never ran init, CLI search/facts nudges me once per run.
expected_behaviour: When settings.json exists without starlog, a stderr tip suggests `starlog init`; suppressed for JSON output, STARLOG_NO_NUDGE, and when settings.json is absent/invalid.

user_story: As a user, `starlog doctor` verifies the bundled corpus loads.
expected_behaviour: `[ok] Corpus — 25 manifests loaded` (bundled corpus-free tier).

user_story: As a fresh user, doctor tells me what's missing without failing.
expected_behaviour: MCP + hook + overlays + project agents show [!] warnings pointing at `starlog init`; exit 0 with 'All critical checks passed (N warnings)'.

user_story: As a configured user, doctor actually spawns the MCP server and lists tools.
expected_behaviour: `[ok] Claude Code MCP — <command>` and `[ok] MCP handshake — starlog_search available`; a broken server yields [x] with 'try npm run build or reinstall'.

user_story: As a user with invalid settings.json, doctor flags it precisely.
expected_behaviour: `[x] settings.json — invalid JSON (...) — fix or remove ...` and exit 1.

user_story: As a user, doctor distinguishes every hook failure mode.
expected_behaviour: registered+missing file → [x] 'script file is missing'; file present+unregistered → [!] 'not registered'; syntax error → [x]; healthy → [ok].

user_story: As an org user, doctor shows the wiring and what this project authored.
expected_behaviour: Reports overlay env wiring ([ok]/[!] re-run init), per-file counts (vetting N, discovery N, policy N), and warns on invalid overlay JSON.

user_story: As a user, doctor tells me which ranking tier I'm on — both are OK.
expected_behaviour: Keyless: '[ok] Ranking — keyword ranking — offline...'; with wired key: hosted line; never a warning.

user_story: As an agent client, `starlog mcp` (or node dist/mcp.js) serves MCP over stdio.
expected_behaviour: initialize → tools/list returns exactly starlog_search and starlog_facts with their schemas; stdout carries only JSON-RPC.

user_story: As an agent, I call starlog_search to discover candidates.
expected_behaviour: Returns markdown per result (Solves/Category/Effort/Best for/Skip when/Stack/Health); no-match returns the honest guidance text; results identical to CLI search (parity).

user_story: As an agent, I call starlog_facts to vet a named package.
expected_behaviour: Returns the same formatFactView text as `starlog facts`; miss returns the honest no-facts message; the tool description is the validated verbatim string.

user_story: As an agent, out-of-range args are rejected by schema.
expected_behaviour: top_k outside 1-50 or wrong types produce an MCP validation error, not a crash.

user_story: As a human whose agent uses starlog, I see the telemetry disclosure in the first tool result.
expected_behaviour: On an unacknowledged install the first tool result appends the one-line disclosure and that call is not recorded; subsequent calls omit it.

feature: No double server on cli mcp
user_story: As a user launching `starlog mcp`, the bundled run-if-main guard must not start a second server.
expected_behaviour: dist/mcp.js auto-starts only when invoked directly (symlink-safe realpath compare); `node dist/cli.js mcp` starts exactly one server.

user_story: As an agent user, installing a known-bad package surfaces its incidents immediately.
expected_behaviour: Hook stdin gets the Bash tool JSON; for `npm install ua-parser-js` it emits hookSpecificOutput additionalContext with KNOWN VULNS/maintenance/license and the 'as of' date.

user_story: As a user installing an uncovered package, it's queued for coverage.
expected_behaviour: Message '[Starlog] No facts on file for ...'; entry appended to ~/.starlog/pending.json and <project>/.starlog/pending.json, deduplicated by manifest_id.

user_story: As a user running ordinary commands, the hook stays silent.
expected_behaviour: `ls`, `npm run build`, `npm test` produce no output; exit 0.

user_story: As a user running compound commands, shell tokens must not be treated as packages.
expected_behaviour: `npm i x && echo done` parses only `x`; flags and invalid names are dropped by the package-name grammar.

user_story: As a Python user, `pip install requests` is detected with pypi naming rules.
expected_behaviour: Ecosystem pypi; version specifiers (==, >=) stripped; facts/queue behavior identical to npm.

user_story: As a user, a hook crash must never fail my tool call.
expected_behaviour: Garbage stdin/JSON → silent exit 0; missing stdin exits after a 3s timeout; queue write failures are swallowed.

user_story: As a user, `starlog telemetry status` shows my current state.
expected_behaviour: Prints enabled/disabled, the anonymous id, config path (~/.starlog/telemetry.json), and opt-out options; exit 0.

user_story: As a user, `starlog telemetry disable` is a persistent opt-out.
expected_behaviour: State file updated (enabled:false); status then reports disabled; enable reverses it; unknown action → error exit 1.

user_story: As a privacy-conscious user, DO_NOT_TRACK=1 / STARLOG_TELEMETRY=0 / CI must silence telemetry.
expected_behaviour: resolveEnabled short-circuits: flag > DO_NOT_TRACK > STARLOG_TELEMETRY > CI/VITEST guard > persisted state; nothing sent when off.

user_story: As a new user, the first tracked command shows me exactly what's collected.
expected_behaviour: TELEMETRY_NOTICE printed once to stderr; re-shown only when NOTICE_VERSION increases (disclosure broadened).

user_story: As a user, my emails/tokens/paths/IPs never reach analytics.
expected_behaviour: scrubText replaces emails, bearer/gh/sk/AKIA tokens, windows+unix absolute paths, IPv4s, and long base64 blobs with ‹redacted›; benign queries pass through.

user_story: As an org user, my private package names are never sent.
expected_behaviour: MCP facts/search event props redact org-private package names to a boolean (mcp-telemetry.ts).

user_story: As a user without a key, `starlog facts push` must refuse clearly.
expected_behaviour: `facts push needs STARLOG_API_KEY (the org key these facts belong to).`; exit 1.

user_story: As a user pointing push at a missing file, I get a clean error.
expected_behaviour: `facts push: no file at <path>` (default .starlog/facts.json); exit 1; invalid overlays are skipped with a count; invalid policy warns 'not pushed'.

user_story: As an org admin with a key, push uploads overlays and my adopted policy.
expected_behaviour: POSTs to the hosted API (policy first when present, then L2); success prints 'Pushed N L2 overlay(s) [+ org policy]'; API failure → error + exit 1; exits explicitly (no hang).

user_story: As a user, `starlog --version` and `--help` orient me.
expected_behaviour: Version matches package.json (0.7.0); help lists all commands with the vet-first description.

user_story: As a user, no starlog error ever shows an unhandled stack trace.
expected_behaviour: All async action errors route through fail(): `starlog: <context>: <hint>`; exit 1; unknown commands get commander's error.

user_story: As a user, the shipped corpus must be complete and valid.
expected_behaviour: 25 discovery manifests across 7 categories all pass schema; 42 L2 fact packages; invalid/unreadable manifest files are skipped with a stderr warning, never abort the load.

user_story: As a maintainer, build, typecheck and the full vitest suite pass from a clean clone.
expected_behaviour: `npm run build` (gen:facts + esbuild), `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run` all succeed without API keys.
